paper.title: Model Selection for Generic Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection for generic stochastic contextual bandits, finite nested function classes (ETC)
unmapped: learner is given a nested family F_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ F_M of finite regressor classes and does not know the smallest realizable class index d*
separability: classes not containing f* have excess risk at least Delta (Assumption 2)
access to an offline least-squares regression oracle
settings.definition_quote: At time $t$, nature picks $(x_t,r_t)$ in an i.i.d fashion from an unknown distribution $D(x,r)$ ... $r_t: \mathcal{A}\rightarrow [0,1]$ ... we are given  a nested class of $M$ function classes, $\mathcal{F}_1 \subset \mathcal{F}_2 \subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{F}_M$.

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection for generic stochastic contextual bandits, finite nested function classes (ACB)
unmapped: learner is given a nested family F_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ F_M of finite regressor classes and does not know the smallest realizable class index d*
separability: classes not containing f* have excess risk at least Delta (Assumption 2)
access to an offline least-squares regression oracle
settings.definition_quote: At time $t$, nature picks $(x_t,r_t)$ in an i.i.d fashion from an unknown distribution $D(x,r)$ ... we are given  a nested class of $M$ function classes, $\mathcal{F}_1 \subset \mathcal{F}_2 \subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{F}_M$.

settings.name_in_paper: Generic contextual bandits with infinite nested function classes (ETC)
unmapped: nested compact (possibly infinite) regressor classes F_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ F_M, unknown smallest realizable index d*
offline regression oracle with estimation error rate xi_{F,delta}(n) (Assumption 4)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the function classes $\mathcal{F}_1 \subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{F}_M$ are compact.

settings.name_in_paper: Generic contextual bandits with infinite nested function classes (ACB)
unmapped: nested compact (possibly infinite) regressor classes, unknown smallest realizable index d*
offline regression oracle with estimation error rate xi_{F,delta}(n) known to the learner (used in learning rate)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the function classes $\mathcal{F}_1 \subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{F}_M$ are compact.

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection for continuum-arm stochastic linear bandits (unknown sparsity)
unmapped: sparsity d* of theta* unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote: The setup comprises of a continuum collection of arms denoted by the set $\mathcal{A}:= \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d:\|x\| \leq 1\}$ ... mean reward ... $\langle x,\theta^* \rangle$, where $\|\theta^*\| \leq 1$. We assume that $\theta^*$ is $d^* \leq d$ sparse ... $\eta_t$ ... sub-gaussian random variables with known parameter $\sigma^2$.

settings.name_in_paper: Dimension model selection for finite-armed linear contextual bandits (nested feature maps)
unmapped: nested known feature maps phi^1,...,phi^M of dimensions d_1<...<d_M; theta* nonzero exactly on first d_{m*} coordinates, d_{m*} unknown
features phi^M(x,a) sub-Gaussian with known parameter tau^2; Sigma_M has positive minimum eigenvalue
settings.definition_quote: At each time $t \in [T]$, the forecaster is shown a context $X_t \in \mathcal{X}$ ... i.i.d. with $X_t \sim \mathcal{D}$, a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$ that is known to the forecaster ... reward $Y_t := \langle \theta^*, \phi^M(X_t,A_t) \rangle + \eta_t$.

algorithms.name: ETC for model selection (with A_CB = FALCON)
Adaptive Contextual Bandits (ACB) with A_CB = FALCON
ALB-Dim (Adaptive Linear Bandit - Dimension, OFUL base)

symbols.F_dstar: cardinality of the smallest realizable class F_{d*}

conditions: Realizability (Assumption 1) and separability with gap Delta (Assumption 2)

source.label: thm:etc
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{asm:second_moment} and \ref{asm:gap} hold. Then with probability at least $1-4M\delta$, running Algorithm~\ref{algo:main_algo} for $T$ iterations yield $R(T) \leq  C \,\, \sqrt{T} + R_{\mathcal{A}_{CB}(\mathcal{F}_{d^*})} (T-2\sqrt{T})$ ... In particular, if $\cb =$ FALCON, with probability at least $1-4M\delta-\delta$, we obtain $R(T) \leq C \sqrt{T} + \mathcal{O} \left(\sqrt{KT \log(|\mathcal{F}_{d^*}|T/\delta)}\right).$

results.notes: Generic black-box form R <= C sqrt(T) + R_{A_CB(F_d*)}(T-2sqrt T) also stated; recorded the FALCON instantiation. Horizon condition comes from Lemma 1 (implicitly required). Delta here is the separation in excess risk, not an arm gap; it only enters the condition.

symbols.Delta_sep: separability gap of Assumption 2 (excess squared risk of the largest non-realizable class)
symbols.F_M: cardinality of the largest class F_M
symbols.F_dstar: cardinality of the smallest realizable class F_{d*}

source.label: thm:falcon
source.quote: Suppose the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:falcon_model} hold. Then with probability at least $1-2M\delta$, running Algorithm~\ref{algo:gen} for $T$ iterations yield $R(T) \leq C \max\{\frac{\log T}{\Delta^2}, \log (|\mathcal{F}_{M}|), \log (1/\delta)\} + R_{\cb(\mathcal{F}_{d^*})}(T)$ ... In particular, if $\cb =$ FALCON, with probability at least $1-2M\delta-\delta$, we obtain ...

results.notes: Generic black-box form also stated. Remark 6: with known T and delta_m = delta/log T, the first term becomes max{1/Delta^2, log|F_M|, log(log T/delta)} (not recorded separately as it's a remark). Δ not needed by the algorithm.

bound.regime: T \gtrsim (log T) max(T^{1/4} xi_{F_M,1/T^{1/4}}, Delta^{-4}, log(1/delta))

symbols.xi_dstar: oracle estimation error xi_{F_{d*}, delta/2T}(T) from Assumption 4

source.label: thm:etc_inf
source.quote: (\texttt{ETC} with $\cb$ = FALCON) Suppose Assumptions~\ref{asm:second_moment}, \ref{asm:sep_inf} and \ref{asm:pred_error_inf} hold. Then, provided, $T \gtrsim (\log T) \max \left(  T^{1/4} \xi_{\mathcal{F}_M, (1/T^{1/4})} , \Delta^{-4}, \log(1/\delta) \right)$, ... with probability at least $1-2M\delta -\delta$, the regret $R(T) \leq C \sqrt{T} + \mathcal{O} \left (\sqrt{K \xi_{\mathcal{F}_{d^*},\delta/2T}(T)} \,\, T \right).$

results.notes: Bound expressed via oracle rate xi; with xi ~ d/T it is sqrt(K d T).

tuning: A_CB = FALCON with rho_m = (1/30) sqrt(K/xi_{F_l^m, delta/2m^2}(tau_{m-1}-tau_{m-2}))

source.label: thm:falcon_inf
source.quote: (\texttt{ACB} with $\cb$ = FALCON) Suppose Assumptions~\ref{asm:second_moment}, \ref{asm:sep_inf} and \ref{asm:pred_error_inf} hold. Then, with probability at least $1-2M\delta-\delta$, running Algorithm~\ref{algo:falcon} for $T$ iterations yield $R(T) \leq C (\log T)  \max\{ \max_m  2^{m/2} \, \xi_{\mathcal{F}_M,1/2^{m/2}}(2^{m-2}), \log (1/\delta), \Delta^{-2} \} + \mathcal{O}\left (\sqrt{K \xi_{\mathcal{F}_{d^*},\delta/2T}(T)} \, T \right).$

bound.expression: c_alg*T_0/gamma**5.18 + C_1*sqrt(T)*(1 + sqrt(s_sparse*log(1 + T/s_sparse))*(1 + sigma*sqrt(log(T/(T_0*delta)) + s_sparse*log(1 + T/s_sparse))))

symbols.T_0: initial phase length defined by Eq. (T_0_defn), O(d^2 ln^2(1/delta))
symbols.gamma: minimum magnitude of nonzero coordinate of theta*

conditions: action set is the unit Euclidean ball

source.label: thm:adaptive_dimension
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm \ref{algo:main_algo_dimensions_unknown} is run with input parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $T_0$ as given in Equation (\ref{eqn:T_0_defn}), then with probability at-least $1-\delta$, the regret after a total of $T$ arm-pulls satisfies $R_T \leq C \frac{T_0}{{\gamma^{5.18}}}T_0 + C_1 \sqrt{T} \bigg [ 1 +   \sqrt{d^*\ln ( 1 + \frac{T}{d^*} )} \times (1 + \sigma\sqrt{ \ln ( \frac{T}{T_0\delta} ) + d^* \ln ( 1+\frac{T}{d^*})})\bigg ].$

results.notes: Printed statement has a duplicated T_0 factor (T_0/gamma^{5.18} T_0); the proof yields T_0 * 2/gamma^{5.18}, so recorded T_0/gamma^5.18 (likely typo). d* is the sparsity of theta* (s_sparse).

symbols.gamma: minimum magnitude of nonzero coordinate of theta*

conditions: action set is the unit Euclidean ball
tuning: T_0 = O~(d^2 ln^2(1/delta)) as in Eq. (eqn:T_0_defn)

source.label: cor:dimension_adaptation
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm \ref{algo:main_algo_dimensions_unknown} is run with input parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $T_0 = \widetilde{O} \left(d^2\ln^2 \left( \frac{1}{\delta} \right) \right)$ given in Equation (\ref{eqn:T_0_defn}), then with probability at-least $1-\delta$, the regret after $T$ times satisfies $R_T \leq O ( \frac{d^2}{{\gamma^{5.18}}} \ln^2 ( d/\delta) )  + \widetilde{O} ( d^* \sqrt{ T}).$

results.notes: Mixed O / O~ notation; recorded as O_tilde.

bound.expression_latex: R_T \leq C T_0  \frac{1}{{\gamma^{5.18}}}  +  (1 + \ln(2K T \ln T))^{3/2} \sqrt{T d_{m^*}} + \sqrt{T}

symbols.T_0: initial phase length from Eq. (eqn:T_0_defn_foster), O(d^2 ln^2(1/delta) tau^2 ln(TK/delta))
symbols.gamma: minimum magnitude of nonzero coordinate of beta*

conditions: features phi^M(x,a) sub-Gaussian with parameter tau^2
tuning: SupLinRel base with feature scaling b(delta)

source.label: thm:adaptive_dimension_foster
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm \ref{algo:main_algo_dimensions_foster} is run with input parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $T_0$ as given in Equation (\ref{eqn:T_0_defn_foster}), then with probability at-least $1-\delta$, the regret after a total of $T$ arm-pulls satisfies $R_T \leq C T_0  \frac{1}{{\gamma^{5.18}}}  +  (1 + \ln(2K T \ln T))^{3/2} \sqrt{T d_{m^*}} + \sqrt{T}.$

results.notes: Regret defined with expectation over contexts in the setup but bound stated w.p. 1-delta; recorded as high-probability. Algorithm uses T through b(delta).

symbols.gamma: minimum magnitude of nonzero coordinate of theta*

tuning: T_0 = O~(d^2 ln^2(1/delta)) as in Eq. (eqn:T_0_defn_foster)

source.label: cor:dimension_adaptation_foster
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm \ref{algo:main_algo_dimensions_foster} is run with input parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $T_0 = \widetilde{O} \left(d^2\ln^2 \left( \frac{1}{\delta} \right) \right)$ given in Equation (\ref{eqn:T_0_defn_foster}) , then with probability at-least $1-\delta$, the regret after $T$ times satisfies $R_T \leq O \left( \frac{d^2}{{\gamma^{5.18}}} \ln^2 ( d/\delta) \tau^2 \ln \left( \frac{TK}{\delta}\right) \right)  + \widetilde{O} (  \sqrt{ T d^*_m}).$

results.notes: Corollary 4 in the appendix restates the same bound.
